subject: Regional compensation band harmonization — proposal and benchmarking questions
summary: Request to align regional compensation bands across US, EU, and APAC; asks for external benchmark clarifications and a proposed approach to apply local multipliers vs fixed bands.
messages:
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, talentanalytics@benchmarks.co
Cc: mercer@example.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional compensation band harmonization — proposal and benchmarking questions

Team,

Following up from last week's pay-committee meeting: we need a pragmatic path to harmonize our leveling bands across US, EU, and APAC for FY27 offers. Current problem: inconsistent local anchors are producing wide offer variance and slowing approvals for EMEA/APAC hires.

Attached is a working model (2026_geo_band_modeling.xlsx) showing two approaches:
- Fixed global bands with location multipliers applied at offer time
- Region-specific anchored bands with narrower local slopes

Questions for Benchmarks/Consultants (cc'd):
1) For enterprise SDE and senior IC roles, what is the typical variance between 25th and 75th percentile across NA vs EU vs APAC (benchmarks by function)?
2) Given a hybrid approach (global band + local index), what sample size / data granularity do you need to validate multipliers?
3) Are there best-practice guardrails for mid-year adjustments when currency movement >8%?

Ask: please review the attached model and the Mercer sample PDF, then provide an initial recommendation and any additional data you need by Wednesday 8/11 EOD. We need this to finalize offer guidance and a headcount Q3 gating rule.

Thanks — I know this is tight. I propose a short sync Thursday to agree on the recommendation to take to the pay committee.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Head of Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026_geo_band_modeling.xlsx (spreadsheet), Mercer_sample_benchmarks.pdf (reference)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: talentanalytics@benchmarks.co, mercer@example.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Regional compensation band harmonization — proposal and benchmarking questions

Jasmine — quick reactions:

• The model looks useful; I like the side-by-side comparator for "global band + multiplier" vs localized bands.
• For committee sign-off we should include an "operational offers" example: 3 live offer scenarios (SDE II, Senior PM, Staff SWE) with final cost delta under each approach. Can Marissa run 3 examples from the current req list?
• On sample size: Mercer told us last year that at least n=50 role-matched data points per region gives reasonable confidence for percentiles; if below that we should fall back to global index + market adjustment.

Two asks for the benchmarks vendor: please confirm whether their dataset treats "remote-hire" as separate from local-headcount for market indexing. That materially changes multipliers for APAC hires who are remote but paid to US market.

I can loop in Finance/Comp ops if we need quick costing. Also recommend we pre-authorize a narrow variance band (+/- 7% on offer) for managers to approve without committee review.

Karthik
VP, People Operations

From: Ben Harrow <talentanalytics@benchmarks.co>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: mercer@example.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 08:27:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Regional compensation band harmonization — proposal and benchmarking questions

Hi Jasmine / team — thanks for the clear brief and the model. A few clarifications from our side before we produce recommendations: 

1) Target percentile: are you aiming to be market-competitive (50th), growth-attract (65th), or retention-focused (75th)? Our recommended multipliers shift materially depending on that goal.
2) Role matching: we match by function+level+product cadence; please confirm whether you want to include equity as part of total cash benchmarking or treat it separately.
3) Remote hires: we can separate remote-set data, but we need a flag in your HR export that distinguishes remote-pay vs local-pay; without that we will map hires to the office location on record.

Preliminary takeaway from a quick skim: APAC median for the roles in your sample is ~38% below US median at 50th percentile, but that compresses to 22% when adjusting for cost-of-living and remote-hire premiums. EU medians sit around 12% below US at 50th.

We will prepare: a) percentile delta table (25/50/75) by region, b) recommended multipliers for a global-band+index approach, and c) three worked offer examples as Karthik asked. Expect deliverable Wednesday 8/11 EOD. 

Link to our initial export: https://benchmarks.co/share/redwood-geo-extract (private link)

Best,
Ben Harrow
Director, Data & Benchmarks
Benchmarks Co.

Attachment: Benchmarks_sample_extract.csv

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

Thanks everyone — good progress. Quick summary and next steps: 

• Benchmarks to deliver full table (25/50/75) + three worked examples by EOD (Ben confirmed).
• Marissa to produce the three operational offer cases (SDE II, Senior PM, Staff SWE) by Tue 8/17 — use the current reqs in Greenboard.
• Karthik to draft the pre-authorization variance policy (+/- 7%) and a short one-pager for pay committee.
• I will consolidate into a one-pager recommendation and circulate to pay committee (Laura to review before circulation).

We will include a fallback rule: if regional sample size < 40 role-matched datapoints, default to global-band + index multiplier and escalate to comp ops for exceptions.

Please add any missing items. If all good, I'll schedule a 30-min pay-committee pre-read sync Thursday 8/13 at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Head of Talent Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Mercer_sample_benchmarks.pdf, 2026_geo_band_modeling.xlsx
